audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings may mix parent and consolidated claims
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical OE numerator and the fully exchanged share denominator may represent different equity claims, distorting the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, the Company consolidates Pla-Fit Holdings’ financial results and reports a non-controlling interest related to the portion of Holdings Units not owned by the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied audit identifies consolidated add-backs combined with parent-attributable income and attributable-income gaps above 5% in seven years. That is a demonstrated methodological inconsistency affecting most observations used for the $210.0 million anchor, although the supplied record lacks yearly amounts needed to quantify the valuation effect. Direction cannot be established without proportionately rebuilding every OE component.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2025 OE on both a fully exchanged consolidated basis and a Planet Fitness, Inc.-attributable basis, recompute the log-trend anchor, and rerun all scenarios if the anchor changes.

audit_findings.title: The TRA liability and related tax benefits may be treated asymmetrically
audit_findings.magnitude: $361.366 million liability at 2026-06-30, equal to $4.75 per diluted share and 9.6% of base equity value; matching realizable tax benefits are not isolated
audit_findings.mechanism: TRA payments must either remain charged through OE taxes or enter the equity bridge net of matching realizable tax benefits.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we recognized $415.8 million of liabilities relating to our obligations under the tax benefit arrangements.
audit_findings.explanation: No error is yet demonstrated because excluding the liability can be coherent when OE retains the full book-tax burden without adding deferred taxes back. If OE instead reflects cash taxes or adds back deferred tax expense, the omitted $361.366 million contractual claim is large enough to change the valuation conclusion. The reported $375.7 million net deferred-tax asset does not identify the portion matching the TRA obligation.
audit_findings.action: Roll the TRA liability and associated deferred-tax assets to June 30, 2026, trace deferred taxes and TRA payments through every OE year, and rerun the bridge with only the net burden if OE does not already charge it.

audit_findings.title: Recurring club refurbishment may be understated as maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.829 million of 2025 existing-club capital expenditures, equal to 38.5% of the $210.0 million anchor; recurring portion and technology spending are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring refurbishment, equipment replacement, or sustaining technology spending omitted from maintenance capex directly overstates OE and may also overstate growth supported by retained cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Corporate-owned clubs require significant upfront and ongoing investment, including periodic remodeling and equipment replacement.
audit_findings.explanation: Understatement is not demonstrated because the maintenance-capex input and composition of the $80.829 million pool were not supplied. Nevertheless, the filed existing-club expenditure pool is sufficiently large relative to anchor OE that an omitted recurring portion is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the maintenance-capex schedule to the 2025 fixed-asset ledger, separating recurring remodels, replacement equipment, sustaining technology and support-center replacement from expansion spending; then rebuild OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Separately added equity-method stakes may still affect the OE numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed equity-method losses were $1.994 million, $4.042 million and $2.840 million in 2023-2025, respectively—1.0%, 1.6% and 1.1% of corresponding OE; the bridge adds $58.4 million of stakes
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained investee earnings or losses affect OE while the separately added stake value enters the bridge, causing duplication; losses understate value and earnings overstate it.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company records its interest in the net earnings of its equity method investees along with adjustments for unrealized profits or losses on intra-entity transactions and amortization of basis differences, within losses from equity-method investments, net of tax in the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The purge remains unverified, but the filed 2023-2025 numerator amounts are each no more than 1.6% of the corresponding OE observation and therefore are not reasonably capable, on the supplied record, of changing the valuation conclusion. Direction is mixed because the known periods contain losses while other periods could contain earnings or different tax and basis-amortization effects.
audit_findings.action: Trace equity-method earnings, losses, basis-difference amortization and related taxes through every OE year and remove them without removing operating royalties or equipment transactions; confirm the recomputed anchor remains effectively unchanged.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 disposal gain may remain in normalized OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.4 million, equal to 2.5% of 2025 OE; even removing the full pretax amount leaves $252.1 million of latest OE, $42.1 million above the $210.0 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A retained nonrecurring gain raises 2025 OE and slightly raises the log-trend anchor; it does not determine the latest-versus-trend minimum directly because the trend is already lower.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction resulted in a gain on sale of corporate-owned clubs of $ 6.4 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, which was included in other (gain) loss, net on the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention has not been demonstrated, but its maximum stated one-year scale is small. Removing the entire filed gain would not make latest OE bind the anchor and affects only one of ten trend observations, so it is not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the gain and insurance recovery through the 2025 OE calculation, remove any retained after-tax nonrecurring amount, and confirm the recomputed trend anchor and scenario values.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated advertising-fund cash is not freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 included: the $400.758 million bridge equals $298.265 million cash plus $102.493 million short-term securities, while $9.556 million of NAF restricted assets is separately reported
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted NAF cash would overstate the cash bridge if included as distributable equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The use of amounts received by the NAFs are restricted to advertising, product development, public relations, merchandising, and administrative expenses and programs to increase sales and further enhance the public reputation of the Planet Fitness brand.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 30, 2026 filed presentation demonstrates that the bridge excludes the separately classified $9.556 million of NAF restricted assets. The identified NAF issue therefore causes no valuation error. Whether other cash is operationally committed remains an unquantified separate possibility, not a demonstrated defect in this finding.
audit_findings.action: Preserve the reconciliation excluding NAF restricted assets and separately document any other legally restricted or operationally committed balances before finalizing excess cash.
